perspective:
Angela Hwang’s available information:

- She knows she is Angela Hwang, an Asian woman, a hairdresser with a doctorate, and has an ISFP personality.
- She knows Kevin Flores has been her friend since high school.
- She knows Kevin works as a construction worker. She noticed he seemed unhappy with his job, so she invited him to coffee.
- At coffee, she heard Kevin say he was “alright” but stuck in the usual grind. He then told her he was not happy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was just going through the motions. He said he had thought about change but didn’t know where to start and felt overwhelmed. She offered to figure it out together/look into options; Kevin agreed and thanked her.
- She believed Kevin was considering a career change and felt supportive and hopeful. She found job openings and a career counseling service, then shared them with Kevin. Kevin thanked her and said he had been thinking a lot; he was interested in something creative, maybe design or architecture. She encouraged him to check the resources; he said he would.
- She believed Kevin was hesitant and felt frustrated and worried. She arranged a meeting with a career coach and told Kevin. Kevin said she didn’t have to, appreciated it, but wasn’t sure he was ready. She encouraged him; he agreed to give it a shot and thanked her.
- She believed Kevin was making progress and felt proud and relieved. She checked in with him. Kevin told her the coach was helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident. She offered more help; he said her support was enough and he would ask if needed.
- She believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career and felt happy and satisfied. She organized a small celebration party. Kevin thanked her and said he was grateful and couldn’t have done it without her. She said he did the hard work and invited him to enjoy the party.
- She does not have access to Kevin’s private inner states, unspoken thoughts, or narrator-only facts beyond what he told her or what she herself believed, felt, or did.
